picks.t: My Morning Jacket – Fillmore Residency (Final Weekend)
picks.d: Nights 5, 6, and 7 of an absolutely legendary seven-night stand at the Fillmore. MMJ blends psychedelic rock, alt-country, and pure soul into shows that feel genuinely once-in-a-lifetime — this is the last chance to catch this run, and SF rock fans will be talking about it for years.

picks.t: Oh, Mary! – Opening Week at the Curran
picks.d: The Tony Award-winning dark comedy everyone's been buzzing about just landed in SF for its opening week, with press night on Thursday the 15th. Think Mary Todd Lincoln, chaos, and the kind of sharp-edged humor that makes you laugh and then feel slightly bad about it — in the best possible way.

The Blue Angels screaming over the bay is one of those quintessential SF moments that never gets old. Head to the Marina Green or anywhere along the northern waterfront, bring snacks, and just look up — it's one of the biggest free spectacles of the entire year.

A Puerto Rican pop legend bringing decades of smash hits to Chase Center for one night only — if you grew up with Chayanne on the radio, this is the one. Even if you didn't, trust us: the energy in that room is going to be something else.

The parade kicks off at Fisherman's Wharf and winds through North Beach to Washington Square — floats, music, community groups, and a whole lot of civic pride. Combine it with the Fleet Week air show for what might be the best free Sunday in SF all year.

Sita Michelle Coltrane leads a special tribute to her mother, the pioneering jazz harpist and spiritual music icon Alice Coltrane, at one of SF's most beloved intimate venues. This is a genuinely rare and moving evening — the kind of show you'll tell people about.

picks.t: RM x SFMOMA: Between You and Me
picks.d: BTS's RM co-curated this exhibition with SFMOMA, bringing together 200 works — including pieces never before shown publicly in the US — spanning Korean modern artists and international heavyweights. Whether you're an ARMY or just an art lover, this one's genuinely special.
Lantern-lit stalls, street food vendors, and live performances winding through one of the country's most historic Chinatowns — this is a free Friday night that feels genuinely magical. Come hungry.

picks.t: Best Friends Podcast Live: Nicole Byer & Sasheer Zamata
picks.d: Nicole Byer and Sasheer Zamata bring their beloved podcast to life on stage at Cobb's — and tickets are almost gone. These two have incredible chemistry, zero filter, and a gift for making a room of strangers feel like a group of old friends.

picks.t: Lucania – New Italian Spot at the Ferry Building
picks.d: From the A16 team, this southern Italian newcomer just opened in the Ferry Building's most coveted space — think marinated anchovies, roasted sardines, and a 140-seat dog-friendly patio right on the Embarcadero. Little fish, big moment.

One of the fastest-rising stars in Latin music right now, Young Miko's reggaeton and Latin trap sound hits different live. Chase Center is going to be electric on Thursday night, and at $59 to start it's the most accessible arena show of the week.

Adults-only Thursday nights at the Exploratorium are always a vibe, and this week's theme — decoding hidden patterns in communication — sounds way more fun than a therapy session. 700+ interactive exhibits, drinks, and real conversation starters all over Pier 15.

picks.t: Terror Vault: SLASHED – Return to Hellville
picks.d: SF's most iconic haunted attraction is back inside the stunning historic San Francisco Mint — theatrical, immersive, and genuinely creepy in ways that feel earned. Get your Halloween season officially started.

ongoing.t: Treasures of the Pharaohs – de Young Museum
ongoing.d: 130 royal treasures on loan from Cairo and Luxor spanning 3,000 years — free for Bay Area residents on Saturdays. Open through Jan 31.

ongoing.t: Alfred Hitchcock's North by Northwest – ACT
ongoing.d: Emma Rice's riotously funny theatrical adaptation closes Oct 18 — this is genuinely the last week to catch it.

ongoing.t: Ha Chong-Hyun: Retrospective – Asian Art Museum
ongoing.d: A major survey of the Korean painter's work, up through January 25. Free first Sunday of the month.

ongoing.t: The Compton's Cafeteria Riot – Tenderloin Museum
ongoing.d: Powerful immersive exhibition on the 1966 uprising, a key moment in trans and LGBTQ+ history. Through Oct 24, ~$7.
The 7 Fingers circus show about SF's history holds a 4.9-star rating and runs multiple nights weekly. From $87.

ongoing.t: Art Before Dishes – Minnesota Street Project
ongoing.d: Free contemporary art exhibition in Dogpatch through October 31 — great excuse to explore this neighborhood.

new.name: Lucania
new.d: From the A16 team: little fish, big patio, stunning Ferry Building location. Dog-friendly and already buzzy.

new.name: Shinka
new.d: Jean-Georges alum Fumio Yonezawa riffs on kaiseki with French technique inside The Jay hotel — mushroom chawanmushi, in-house fermentation, serious vibes.

new.name: Olive Juice
new.d: A converted paint store turned salad-focused café — one of October's most anticipated openings on one of SF's best food streets.

new.name: Bayview Oyster Bar
new.d: Grilled and raw oysters, clam chowder, Dungeness crab with garlic noodles — a soulful new anchor for the Bayview neighborhood.

new.name: Ah Ma's Kitchen
new.d: Yelp's #16 Best New Restaurant in America for 2026 — Hong Kong flavors on Clement Street, and one of only two Bay Area spots on that list.

new.name: Rose Pizzeria
new.d: The New York Times-anointed Berkeley fave just opened its SF outpost in the old Village Pizzeria space — same snappy pies, natural wines, and cult following.

classic.name: A16
classic.d: The OG southern Italian anchor that spawned Lucania — wood-fired pizzas, killer wine list, always reliable.

classic.name: Maillards at Two Pitchers Brewing
classic.d: Legendary SF smashburger pop-up now permanent inside a great taproom — cold beer, crispy beef, ocean air nearby.

classic.name: Delah / Haraz / Heyma
classic.d: SF's Yemeni café scene is thriving — all three are open late (some until 1am weekends), perfect for a non-boozy night cap.

classic.name: La Cigale
classic.d: No tips, no reservations — just walk in, eat something wood-fired, and enjoy one of the friendliest new neighborhood spots in the city.

classic.name: Ferry Building Marketplace
classic.d: Saturday farmers market plus year-round vendors — now with Lucania as a marquee neighbor. A perfect Saturday morning ritual.

bars.name: 15 Romolo
bars.d: The 115-year-old pseudo-speakeasy tucked down an alley in North Beach just reopened after a two-year renovation — Pimm's cups, sherry, and bohemian energy all freshened up.

bars.name: Bar Maritime
bars.d: Part of the city's martini-having-a-moment wave — they infuse vodka with oyster shell flavor and the results are weirdly, perfectly delicious.

bars.name: Super Mensch
bars.d: Lox-and-bagel-inspired martini with caper sherry, tomato water, and a salmon caviar olive — yes, really, and yes, you should.

bars.name: 1015 Folsom
bars.d: SF's legendary 1,400-cap dance institution celebrating its anniversary this Thursday — Tiësto and Fatboy Slim have played here; the sound system is no joke.

bars.name: Public Works
bars.d: Roam Recordings' 25th anniversary party Friday night with Man Power — one of SF's most beloved underground venues doing what it does best.

bars.name: Audio SF
bars.d: 250-capacity room with serious sound — Baauer headlines Friday. Small enough to feel the music in your chest, big enough to actually dance.

bars.name: The Midway
bars.d: Tinlicker headlines Saturday with their melodic techno magic — The Midway's indoor space and production values make this one of the best club nights of the week.

bars.name: Halcyon
bars.d: UK house and afro-percussion from Melé on Friday — Halcyon is a SoMa institution and the room always sounds exactly right for this kind of groove.

games.detail: NBA Preseason — a tune-up before the real thing starts Oct 21

sports.note: Preseason vibes are loose and fun — great time to grab cheap seats and get hyped for the new season.

games.teams: Valkyries vs. Las Vegas Aces — WNBA Semifinals Game 4 (if necessary)
games.detail: GS already won Game 1 71–60. A Finals berth is on the line.

sports.note: This is must-see playoff basketball. The Valkyries are for real and Chase Center is going to be LOUD.

games.teams: Rod Wave: Don't Look Down Tour
games.detail: Florida's melodic rap storyteller on one of his biggest stages yet

sports.note: Not sports, but Chase Center is the venue — worth noting if you're already heading there Friday.

concerts.d: The final three nights of a seven-show Fillmore residency — psychedelic rock, alt-country, and pure emotional power from one of America's greatest live bands. Each night is a different setlist, so if you can swing multiple nights, do it.
concerts.venue: The Fillmore · ~$232+ resale, check Fillmore for face value

concerts.d: Sita Michelle Coltrane leads an evening honoring her mother's transcendent legacy — jazz, harp, and deeply spiritual music in one of SF's most intimate and beloved rooms. This is a special one.

Melodic rap's most emotionally raw storyteller brings the Don't Look Down Tour to Chase Center. His blend of hip-hop and R&B-soaked introspection hits differently at arena scale — bring your feelings.

Bailemos Otra Vez Tour brings the Puerto Rican pop and Latin dance icon to Chase Center for one night only. Decades of hits, an audience that knows every word, and the kind of communal joy that only the biggest Latin pop stars can generate.

One of Latin music's fastest-rising stars closes the week at Chase Center with her Late Checkout Tour. Her genre-blurring reggaeton and Latin trap sound is built for live shows — energetic, genre-fluid, and genuinely exciting.
The American Idol Season 11 winner and bluesy folk-rock singer plays one of SF's most beloved intimate rooms. His voice sounds even better up close, and GAMH is the perfect size for it.
concerts.venue: Great American Music Hall · Check gamh.com

concerts.d: A post-punk triple bill presented as part of GAMH's Psyched! Fest series — adventurous, abrasive, and exactly the kind of Tuesday night you'll actually remember. At $27.50, it's a steal.

Camilo Lara aka Mexican Institute of Sound blends cumbia, electronica, and Latin pop into one of the most danceable sets you'll find mid-week. Support from Spaghetti Cumbia and friends makes this a full party.
concerts.venue: Great American Music Hall · Check gamh.com

concerts.d: LA's post-punk trio brings cold motorik rhythms and deadpan vocals to The Independent — if you love Suicide, Devo, or Dry Cleaning, this is your Tuesday. Hypnotic, minimal, and genuinely cool.

concerts.t: KAFANA BALKAN with Inspector Gadje Balkan Brass Band
concerts.d: One of SF's most beloved recurring cultural celebrations — raucous Balkan brass, folk-dance energy, and a room full of people who absolutely cannot stay in their seats. Come ready to move.

concertsOngoing.d: Fri Oct 9 + Sat Oct 10 at 7:30pm, Sun Oct 11 at 2pm — Davies Symphony Hall. The master's final orchestral work, sweeping and dramatic.
Mon Oct 12 at 7:30pm — Davies Symphony Hall. Minimalist and meditative; bring someone you want to sit quietly with.
Tue Oct 13 — Davies Symphony Hall. The classics, done right.
Thu Oct 15 at 7:30pm — Davies Symphony Hall. Three world-class soloists sharing one stage — genuinely rare.
Fri Oct 9 — The Independent. Philadelphia soul and R&B with serious velvet vocals.
Fri Oct 9 · Doors 8pm / Show 9pm — Rickshaw Stop. Bay Area bedroom-pop R&B, local favorite, great room.

singles.d: Two back-to-back speed dating sessions at an upscale East Bay venue — no cost to enter, low pressure, and you get to meet a lot of people fast. Pre-Dating runs tight, fun events that feel less awkward than you'd expect.

singles.t: Midweek Date Night at Rick & Roxy's – Cityswoon
singles.d: Cityswoon's smart-matching 'Speed Dating 2.0' comes to the Marina District — their algorithm pairs you based on preferences rather than just who's sitting across from you. Great mid-week option for busy 30s and 40s professionals who want something a little more intentional.

singles.t: Black & Dating: Singles Mixer at DACHA
singles.d: An inclusive mixer centering Black singles, open to all backgrounds, at DACHA Kitchen & Bar in Lower Nob Hill. Good drinks, a welcoming room, and actual conversation starters built into the format — a warm and well-organized way to end the week.

singles.t: Volo Sports – Glow Kickball + Flip Cup League Kickoff
singles.d: Glow-in-the-dark kickball at Dolores Park followed by flip cup — Volo runs the most socially active rec sports leagues in the city and this kickoff night is specifically designed to meet your new favorite people. Come solo, leave with a team group chat.

singles.t: Slow Runners Club – Sunday Morning Run
singles.d: 2,300+ members, zero judgment about pace, and optional coffee afterward — this is genuinely one of SF's friendliest social groups. Starts at Baker & Oak in the Panhandle, ends with the kind of easy conversation that happens when everyone just ran a few miles together.
A more immersive take on singles events at O'Reilly's Pub — designed for people who find conventional speed dating a little stiff. Group date format, more mingling, less musical-chairs energy.

singlesOngoing.t: Run Club SF – Tue & Thu Runs
singlesOngoing.d: Tuesdays at MLK/7th Ave, Thursdays at Kezar Stadium, both at 6:30pm — 'a social club with a running problem.' Free to join.
Saturday Oct 10 at 7:30am — scenic, social, and a natural conversation starter. Register at thebestraces.com.

date.title: Fleet Week + North Beach Sunday
date.tagline: Jets overhead, parade below, pizza after — the perfect SF Sunday

steps.title: Italian Heritage Parade
steps.detail: Catch the parade starting at Fisherman's Wharf and walk it up Columbus into North Beach — floats, music, good crowd energy, and completely free.

steps.title: Fleet Week Air Show from the Waterfront
steps.detail: Head to the northern waterfront or Marina Green — the Blue Angels are overhead and it's one of those SF moments that's genuinely hard to beat.

steps.title: Washington Square Park Hang
steps.detail: Grab a coffee from a nearby café, find a patch of grass, and just sit. Post-parade, post-air show, the park has a great lingering energy.

steps.title: Dinner at Rose Pizzeria (Inner Richmond)
steps.detail: End the day at the new SF outpost of the NYT-anointed Berkeley pie legend — snappy thin crust, natural wines, no reservations needed.

date.title: Exploratorium After Dark + SoMa Drinks
date.tagline: Adults-only science, cocktails, and actual things to talk about

steps.title: Exploratorium After Dark: Speak Easy
steps.detail: Pier 15 goes adults-only Thursday night — the Speak Easy theme is all about communication and hidden patterns, which honestly makes for great date conversation. ~$19–30/person.

steps.title: Walk the Embarcadero
steps.detail: Post-museum, take a slow walk along the waterfront — it's beautiful at night and completely free.

steps.title: Drinks at Bar Maritime
steps.detail: Oyster shell-infused vodka martinis and a cozy FiDi-adjacent bar. Order the martini, explain how it's made, watch the reaction.

date.title: SFMOMA + Shinka Dinner
date.tagline: World-class art, world-class food, memorable evening

steps.title: RM x SFMOMA: Between You and Me
steps.detail: Spend a couple hours with the RM-curated exhibition on Floor 7 — 200 works including pieces never before shown in the US. ~$25/person, and it's genuinely worth it.

steps.title: Walk to The Jay Hotel
steps.detail: It's a short walk from SFMOMA to Battery Street in FiDi — good time to decompress and talk about what you saw.

steps.title: Dinner at Shinka
steps.detail: Chef Fumio Yonezawa's Japanese-French kaiseki debut — mushroom chawanmushi, in-house fermentation, stunning plating. One of the most exciting new restaurants in the city right now.

solo.title: Indigenous Peoples' Day at Yerba Buena
solo.tagline: A meaningful Monday that costs nothing

steps.title: YBG Dance Day (if you missed Sunday)
steps.detail: Yerba Buena Gardens Festival's free outdoor dance celebration — local troupes, open park, welcoming energy.

steps.title: Indigenous Peoples' Day Celebration
steps.detail: International Indian Treaty Council and YBGF present a free cultural event at Yerba Buena Gardens featuring Jeremy Dutcher — genuinely moving and important.

steps.title: Wander SoMa
steps.detail: Walk off the afternoon through SoMa — SFMOMA is right there if you want to pop in, or just grab a coffee and sit with your thoughts.

solo.title: Jazz Tribute at GAMH
solo.tagline: A Sunday evening that feeds the soul

steps.title: Early Dinner in the Tenderloin
steps.detail: Grab dinner nearby before the show — the Tenderloin has great affordable spots and The Compton's Cafeteria Riot exhibit at 835 Larkin is only $7 if you want some context and history first.

steps.title: Doors at Great American Music Hall
steps.detail: Arrive early for Divine Offering: Celebrating Alice Coltrane — get a drink, find a good spot, soak in the room. GAMH is one of the most beautiful venues in the city.

steps.title: Sita Michelle Coltrane performs
steps.detail: Let the music do its thing. Alice Coltrane's spiritual jazz is the kind of thing that reorganizes something in your chest — her daughter leading this tribute makes it even more special. $39.50–$45.

solo.title: My Morning Jacket at the Fillmore
solo.tagline: The kind of night you'll be telling people about

steps.title: Dinner at A16
steps.detail: The Fillmore is in the Western Addition — A16 on Chestnut is a short Lyft away and one of the city's best Italian spots. Get the pizza and a glass of something southern Italian.

steps.title: Arrive at The Fillmore
steps.detail: Grab a poster — the Fillmore prints limited-edition show posters and a MMJ residency night is one worth framing. Get a drink, find your spot on the floor.

steps.title: My Morning Jacket plays
steps.detail: Let it wash over you. Night 5, 6, or 7 of the residency — each has a different setlist, and the band plays with a looseness and joy that only comes from a full week in one room. This is the one.

birthday.title: Fleet Week Birthday Bash
birthday.tagline: The city throws you a free air show — you're welcome

steps.title: Meet at the Marina Green
steps.detail: Rally the crew and claim a patch of grass along the northern waterfront. Bring snacks, bring a blanket, bring whoever loves you.

steps.title: Fleet Week Air Show
steps.detail: The Blue Angels do their thing overhead and it genuinely never gets old. Free, spectacular, and very SF.

steps.title: Drinks at 15 Romolo
steps.detail: The newly reopened North Beach speakeasy is the perfect post-air show destination — tucked down a little alley, great cocktails, exactly the right vibe for a birthday afternoon.

birthday.title: Terror Vault + Late Night SoMa
birthday.tagline: Haunted birthday season has officially begun

steps.title: Terror Vault: SLASHED – Return to Hellville
steps.detail: Kick off the birthday night at the San Francisco Mint — SF's most iconic haunted attraction is theatrical, creepy, and a genuinely fun group experience. Book VIP if you want the full treatment.

steps.title: Dinner at La Cigale (Glen Park) or nearby
steps.detail: No-tips, no-reservations wood-fired spot that's perfect for a group — or pick your birthday restaurant of choice and let people come to you.

steps.title: Dance at The Midway or 1015 Folsom
steps.detail: Tinlicker at The Midway Saturday night or 1015 Day Thursday — both are big, loud, and exactly right for a birthday that doesn't end at 10pm.

birthday.title: Chayanne at Chase Center
birthday.tagline: The birthday night with maximum joy and zero irony

steps.title: Pre-Show Dinner at Shinka or Lucania
steps.detail: Start with a proper dinner — Lucania at the Ferry Building for a convivial Italian feast, or Shinka at The Jay for a special-occasion Japanese-French kaiseki experience.

steps.title: Head to Chase Center
steps.detail: Get there early enough to get drinks and soak in the pre-show energy — Chayanne crowds are famously joyful and the anticipation is half the fun.

steps.title: Chayanne: Bailemos Otra Vez
steps.detail: Decades of hits, a sold-out arena of people who know every word, and a performer who treats every show like it might be his last. Happy birthday — this one's on Chayanne.

friends.title: Saturday in the City
friends.tagline: Air show, Chinatown, nowhere to be — perfect Saturday

steps.title: Coffee Lovers Run at Crissy Field (optional)
steps.detail: If the group is ambitious, the 5K/10K fun run starts at 7:30am and ends right where the air show begins. If not, just meet at the Marina Green later.

steps.title: Fleet Week Air Show
steps.detail: Park yourselves on the Marina Green with snacks and watch the Blue Angels. This is peak free SF.

steps.title: Wander down to Chinatown
steps.detail: Make your way to Chinatown in the afternoon — the Night Market kicks off Friday but the neighborhood is worth the Saturday wander too. Dim sum, bubble tea, just walking around.

steps.title: KAFANA BALKAN at the Rickshaw Stop
steps.detail: End the night with raucous Balkan brass and folk dancing at one of SF's most fun recurring events. Check the door price — it's usually very reasonable.

friends.title: Psyched! Fest Tuesday + Late Bites
friends.tagline: A weeknight that earns its place in the group chat

steps.title: Doors at Great American Music Hall
steps.detail: Provoker, Topographies, and Dalmatia as part of GAMH's Psyched! Fest — $27.50 gets you a proper post-punk triple bill. Grab drinks and stake out a spot.

steps.title: Provoker plays
steps.detail: Let the music be loud and good. Bring whoever in the group is always asking why you never do anything interesting on Tuesdays.

steps.title: Late drinks at Super Mensch or nearby
steps.detail: Debrief the show over that salmon caviar martini at Super Mensch, or find a late bar in the neighborhood and let the conversation run.

friends.title: Oh, Mary! Opening Week
friends.tagline: Opening night energy is its own thing entirely

steps.title: Pre-Show Dinner on Geary
steps.detail: The Curran is right in Union Square — plenty of great dinner options nearby. Make a reservation, take your time, let everyone get settled and excited.

steps.title: Oh, Mary! at the Curran Theatre
steps.detail: The Tony Award-winning dark comedy in its opening week in SF — press night is Thursday the 15th. Opening week audiences are the best audiences; the energy is electric.

steps.title: Post-Show Drinks at 15 Romolo
steps.detail: The newly reopened North Beach speakeasy is a short cab ride away and a perfect post-theater spot to argue about the show and order another round.

parents.title: Italian Heritage Sunday with the Whole Family
parents.tagline: History, parades, and free air shows — grandma will love it

steps.title: Brunch in North Beach
steps.detail: Get there early and find a café or bakery on Columbus — North Beach has been feeding families before parades for a century and it's still very good at it.

steps.title: Italian Heritage Parade
steps.detail: Watch from Columbus Avenue as the parade rolls through — floats, community groups, live music, and genuine neighborhood pride. Free, festive, and very SF.

steps.title: Fleet Week Air Show
steps.detail: Walk or drive to the northern waterfront to catch the tail end of the air show. Kids go absolutely wild for the Blue Angels — even if your parents have seen it before, seeing it through kids' eyes makes it new again.

parents.title: de Young + Ferry Building Lunch
parents.tagline: Art, oysters, and a patio the whole family can agree on

steps.title: Farmers Market at the Ferry Building
steps.detail: Saturday morning market is one of SF's best rituals — grab coffee, wander the stalls, pick up something to snack on. Check out the new Lucania patio while you're there.

steps.title: Lunch at Lucania or Ferry Building vendors
steps.detail: Dog-friendly patio, southern Italian food, Embarcadero views — it's a perfect family lunch spot. Saturday is also free for Bay Area residents at the de Young, so factor that into timing.

steps.title: Treasures of the Pharaohs at the de Young
steps.detail: 130 royal treasures from Cairo and Luxor spanning 3,000 years — genuinely fascinating for all ages and free for Bay Area residents on Saturdays. Plenty to talk about on the drive home.

parents.title: SF Symphony + Dinner at A16
parents.tagline: The kind of evening your parents will brag about to their friends

steps.title: Dinner at A16
steps.detail: Start with a proper southern Italian dinner — great wine list, wood-fired pizza, reliably wonderful. The kind of place that impresses parents who eat well and appreciate it.

steps.title: SF Symphony: Rachmaninoff Symphonic Dances
steps.detail: Friday or Saturday night at Davies Symphony Hall — Rachmaninoff's final orchestral work is sweeping and emotionally rich, and the SFS performs it beautifully. Dress up a little.

steps.title: Nightcap at a Civic Center bar
steps.detail: After the Symphony, the neighborhood has good options for a quiet drink and a recap. Let your parents tell you how wonderful it was. Agree, because it was.
